instruction: Highlight the cells in column B containing employee names in the first table if their clock-out time in column D is earlier than 5:00 PM.

metadata.explanation: Task requires highlighting employee names who left before 5:00 PM. Verified with Python: 5 employees left early - Blake Dreary (B13, 16:27), Arnold Shawarma (B15, 16:22), Olivia Calme (B17, 16:11), Kanye East (B22, 16:29), Swan Ronson (B23, 16:28). Custom getter extracts fill information for specified cells, metric checks if all 5 cells have background highlighting applied.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts cell fill/highlighting information from specified cells (B13, B15, B17, B22, B23) using openpyxl library
Metric correctly checks if cells have highlighting by accessing expected.get('highlighted_cells') - parameter handling is correct for type='rule'
Expected values are semantically correct - all 5 cells (B13, B15, B17, B22, B23) correspond to employees who left before 17:00 as verified in metadata
Postconfig appropriately saves file with Ctrl+S before verification to ensure file state is persisted
Partial credit scoring logic is correct - score = correctly_highlighted / total_expected_cells
Data flow is correct: getter extracts fill info -> metric checks has_fill property -> returns proportional score
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor limitation: evaluator doesn't verify that ONLY the correct cells are highlighted (could pass if user highlights additional cells beyond the required ones), but this is acceptable given the instruction wording
Static warning about 'dict vs Dict' type annotation is cosmetic and doesn't affect runtime behavior
